strings.d1.s0.name: Sagrada Família
strings.d1.s0.tips: Gaudí's basilica. Book timed tickets online weeks ahead (centenary year 2026, 26-40 EUR); the tower costs extra. At 09:00 the light hits the stained glass.
strings.d1.s1.name: Casa Batlló
strings.d1.s1.tips: The house with the dragon-back roof. Book online, morning slot.
strings.d1.s2.name: Casa Milà La Pedrera
strings.d1.s2.tips: Admire the wavy facade from the street; the interior is an optional 28 EUR.
strings.d1.s3.name: Cerveseria Catalana
strings.d1.s3.tips: A classic Eixample tapas bar. Order montaditos (small toasts) and gambas; the queue is short at 13:30.
strings.d1.s4.name: Passeig de Gràcia
strings.d1.s4.tips: A modernist boulevard lined with shops.
strings.d1.b0.name: Tapas 24
strings.d1.b0.tips: Carles Abellan's tapas spot; try the bikini sandwich.
strings.d1.b1.name: Recinte Modernista Sant Pau
strings.d1.b1.tips: A modernist hospital complex near the Sagrada Família. Quieter than Casa Batlló.
strings.d2.s0.name: Barcelona Cathedral
strings.d2.s0.tips: A Gothic cathedral with a cloister courtyard of geese. Free entry during the morning Mass.
strings.d2.s1.name: Barri Gòtic Streets
strings.d2.s1.tips: Plaça Sant Felip Neri, the Roman columns (MUHBA Temple d'August, free) and the Bisbe bridge.
strings.d2.s2.name: La Boqueria
strings.d2.s2.tips: The market on La Rambla. Eat squid with eggs at the El Quim or Bar Pinotxo counter; best before 10:00.
strings.d2.s3.name: El Born Santa Maria del Mar
strings.d2.s3.tips: The Cathedral of the Sea, plain and elegant Gothic.
strings.d2.s4.name: Picasso Museum
strings.d2.s4.tips: Early-period Picasso. Free on Thursday evenings; book online.
strings.d2.b0.name: El Xampanyet
strings.d2.b0.tips: Serving cava and anchovies since 1929. Standing only, next to the Picasso Museum.
strings.d2.b1.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
strings.d2.b1.tips: Tour of the modernist concert hall, as an alternative to the Picasso Museum.
strings.d3.s0.name: Park Güell
strings.d3.s0.tips: The mosaic salamander and the wavy bench. Timed tickets online (10 EUR); the first slot at 08:30 is quiet.
strings.d3.s1.name: Bunkers del Carmel
strings.d3.s1.tips: A former anti-aircraft hilltop with Barcelona's best free 360° view.
strings.d3.s2.name: Gràcia Plaça del Sol
strings.d3.s2.tips: A village-like neighbourhood of squares and terraces.
strings.d3.s3.name: La Pubilla Gràcia
strings.d3.s3.tips: Catalan set lunch in Gràcia. Closed on Sundays.
strings.d3.s4.name: Casa Vicens
strings.d3.s4.tips: Gaudí's first house, with tile and palm-leaf motifs, in Gràcia.
strings.d3.b0.name: Bar Bodega Quimet Gràcia
strings.d3.b0.tips: Vermouth and tinned-seafood tapas; a local favourite.
strings.d3.b1.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
strings.d3.b1.tips: A modernist hospital, as an alternative to Casa Vicens.
strings.d4.s0.name: MNAC Museu Nacional
strings.d4.s0.tips: Romanesque frescoes in a palace building. The steps give city views, and the terrace is free.
strings.d4.s1.name: Fundació Joan Miró
strings.d4.s1.tips: Miró's works in Sert's white building.
strings.d4.s2.name: Montjuïc Cable Car
strings.d4.s2.tips: A cable car up to the castle with sea views.
strings.d4.s3.name: Montjuïc Castle Cafe
strings.d4.s3.tips: Lunch in the castle courtyard with a view of the port.
strings.d4.s4.name: Font Màgica Montjuïc
strings.d4.s4.tips: The Magic Fountain's music-and-light show (summer Thursday to Sunday at 21:00). It may be closed for maintenance in winter, so check first.
strings.d4.b0.name: Quimet & Quimet Poble Sec
strings.d4.b0.tips: A legendary tinned-seafood tapas bar in Poble Sec. Standing only.
strings.d4.b1.name: Montjuïc Olympic Stadium
strings.d4.b1.tips: The 1992 stadium, as an alternative to the cable car.
strings.d5.s0.name: Barceloneta Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: The city beach. Quiet in the morning, sunloungers 8 EUR, sea around 25°C in summer.
strings.d5.s1.name: La Cova Fumada
strings.d5.s1.tips: The birthplace of the bomba (potato croquette). No menu, cash only, full by 13:00.
strings.d5.s2.name: Barceloneta Seafront Walk to the W Hotel
strings.d5.s2.tips: A palm-lined seafront stroll that passes Frank Gehry's fish sculpture.
strings.d5.s3.name: Port Vell and Maremagnum
strings.d5.s3.tips: The old harbour, with the Rambla de Mar bridge.
strings.d5.s4.name: Port Cable Car
strings.d5.s4.tips: The red cable car over the harbour to Montjuïc, with views of sea and city.
strings.d5.b0.name: Can Paixano La Xampanyeria
strings.d5.b0.tips: Cava and sandwiches. Standing only, and cheap.
strings.d5.b1.name: Museu d'Història de Catalunya
strings.d5.b1.tips: A history museum in a port warehouse, with a terrace cafe.
strings.d6.s0.name: Montserrat Monastery
strings.d6.s0.tips: Train plus rack railway takes 1.5 hours (about 50 EUR combined ticket). The Black Madonna sits on the serrated mountain; the boys' choir (Escolania) sings at 13:00.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sant Joan Funicular
strings.d6.s1.tips: A funicular to the summit, with walking trails.
strings.d6.s2.name: Montserrat Sant Joan Walk
strings.d6.s2.tips: A flat 1-hour walk among the rocks with views over Catalonia.
strings.d6.s3.name: Montserrat Restaurant Abat Cisneros
strings.d6.s3.tips: The monastery hotel's restaurant, serving a Catalan lunch.
strings.d6.s4.name: Montserrat Market Stalls
strings.d6.s4.tips: Farmers' stalls selling mató (fresh goat's cheese) and honey.
strings.d6.b0.name: Montserrat Self-Service Cafeteria
strings.d6.b1.name: Santa Cova
strings.d6.b1.tips: A path to the cave where the Madonna was found, as an alternative to Sant Joan.
strings.d7.theme: Rambla morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: La Rambla Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Walk the Rambla before the crowds arrive, past the Miró mosaic and the flower stalls.
strings.d7.s1.name: Palau Güell
strings.d7.s1.tips: Gaudí's city mansion, with its rooftop chimneys.
strings.d7.s2.name: Granja Viader
strings.d7.s2.tips: Hot chocolate and churros since 1870, in the dairy where Cacaolat was born.
strings.d7.s3.name: Plaça Reial
strings.d7.s3.tips: A palm-filled square with Gaudí lampposts, ideal for a farewell photo. The Aerobús leaves from Plaça Catalunya.
strings.d7.b0.name: Bar Lobo Raval
strings.d7.b1.name: MACBA Raval
strings.d7.b1.tips: Contemporary art and skateboarders, as an alternative to Palau Güell.
strings.note0: Get a T-casual 10-ride metro ticket; the Aerobús from Plaça Catalunya takes 35 minutes. The city is walkable, and Montjuïc has a cable car and funicular.
strings.note1: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, Casa Batlló and the Picasso Museum: timed online tickets are ESSENTIAL. For the Sagrada Família, book months ahead because of the 2026 centenary.
strings.note2: Summers are 28-32°C, with beaches and terraces. In August many local shops close for holiday; the Font Màgica runs Thursday to Sunday at 21:00.
strings.note3: The set lunch (menú del día) costs 13-18 EUR, about half the price of dinner. Eating standing at a tapas bar is cheap; dinner starts after 21:00.
strings.note4: Pickpocketing on the Rambla and the metro is among the worst in Europe. Keep your bag in front of you and never leave your phone on the table.
strings.note5: Catalan and Spanish are spoken; 'bon dia' is enough. For a tip, round up the bill.
